describes: docs(arch): record the parser decision, ownership, reuse and lineage (#812), 2026-10-09
authority: FWA1's FrameworkActivation record is the only activation source (framework-common Activation). This row is data FWA1 reads; it adds no second activation path.

record.modeRule: The dialect is the record's mode. Each mode is exactly one profile of liquid-version-lock.json; the admitted release of a mode is that profile's release.
record.needSelectionNote: NeedSelection is a per-file outcome of the .liquid association below, not a fifth record state. FWA1 owns how it is carried; this lock fixes only that it is distinct from active, inactive and off and is never resolved by a guess.

precedenceRule: A lower precedence rank wins. Rank 0 is the switch (frameworks.liquid = off or an explicit on naming a release); rank 1 is the automatic sources AP-S1..AP-S4, which never outrank each other and only combine through the association rule; rank 2 is the inactive default.

switch.readThrough: CFG0 declarative capture; no evaluation of user config
switch.explicitOnShape: frameworks.liquid = { state: on, release: <an exact admitted release of one profile> }. The release decodes to exactly one profile, so naming the release names the profile and sets the mode; a release that does not decode is Invalid at capture (CFG0 CR04), and a decoded release that is not admitted is unsupported-version (VID0 R06, FWA1-AC6).

sources.outcome: off for the whole vertical: no parse, no facts, no capability (LIQ3-AC5, LIQP0-AC4)

sources.evidence: a directory that holds both layout/theme.liquid and config/settings_schema.json (the Shopify theme architecture's required files)
sources.readAs: file presence only; neither file is parsed for activation and nothing is executed
sources.admittedRelease: the shopify profile's reference release; a theme vendors no engine, so there is no resolved version to read
sources.fwa1Acceptance: FWA1-AC7 (a theme root gives liquid active in mode shopify)

sources.evidence: the gem jekyll resolved in the package's Gemfile.lock (a `jekyll (<exact version>)` spec under GEM specs)
sources.readAs: Gemfile.lock read as data; no Ruby or bundle process runs (FWA1-AC7 planted-process leg)
sources.scope: the directory holding Gemfile.lock and its descendants
sources.admittedRelease: the resolved exact version when it lies in the jekyll admittedLine; otherwise unsupported-version

sources.evidence: @11ty/eleventy resolved for the package in the PM package graph (PM3 facts)
sources.readAs: resolved package facts; the Eleventy config is never executed
sources.admittedRelease: the resolved exact @11ty/eleventy version when it lies in the eleventy admittedLine, and its resolved liquidjs inside the liquidjs admittedLine; otherwise unsupported-version
sources.subsumes: only the liquidjs that @11ty/eleventy resolves through its own dependency edge is the Eleventy engine and is not a second claim. A liquidjs the package declares itself is an independent AP-S4 claim even when it resolves to the same installed instance: package co-presence proves neither that the instances are one nor that every .liquid file uses the Eleventy profile, so both claims over one file are NeedSelection.

sources.evidence: liquidjs resolved as a direct dependency of the package, whether or not the package also resolves @11ty/eleventy
sources.readAs: resolved package facts; user code calling the engine is never executed
sources.admittedRelease: the resolved exact liquidjs version when it lies in the liquidjs admittedLine; otherwise unsupported-version
sources.narrowing: The charter admits liquidjs resolved in the package graph. This row reads that as a direct dependency: a liquidjs reached only transitively through a dependency other than @11ty/eleventy is that dependency's private engine and says nothing about the package's own .liquid files, the same reason a bare liquid gem names no dialect (AP-N4). Such a package needs an explicit on (AP-S5). A liquidjs reached through @11ty/eleventy is AP-S3's engine.

sources.evidence: frameworks.liquid = { state: on, release: <exact admitted release> }
sources.outcome: active in the mode of the named release's profile, for every .liquid file in the configuration's scope; it also resolves NeedSelection for those files

sources.evidence: none of AP-S1..AP-S5 (frameworks.liquid = auto or unset)
sources.outcome: inactive: a .liquid file classifies to its fallback and no Liquid parse runs (LIQ3-AC5)

neverActivates.evidence: a .liquid file extension, alone or in any number
neverActivates.reason: an extension is presentation, never identity (VID0 R03); the charter forbids extension-only activation

neverActivates.evidence: a <script src> naming a Liquid engine build (for example a CDN liquidjs bundle)
neverActivates.reason: no manifest entry; activation needs an explicit on (FWA1 Switch)

neverActivates.evidence: directory evidence other than the two theme-root files together: snippets/, sections/, blocks/, templates/, locales/, _includes/, _layouts/, _posts/, _config.yml, eleventy.config.*, .eleventy.js, shopify.extension.toml, or only one of the two theme-root files
neverActivates.reason: the only directory evidence the charter admits is the theme root; any other layout is a name match

neverActivates.evidence: the liquid gem resolved in Gemfile.lock without jekyll
neverActivates.reason: the charter's lockfile source is jekyll; a bare engine dependency names no dialect, so it needs an explicit on

neverActivates.evidence: liquidjs resolved only transitively, through a dependency other than @11ty/eleventy
neverActivates.reason: a dependency's private engine names no dialect for the package's files (AP-S4 narrowing); it needs an explicit on

neverActivates.evidence: a dialect chosen from file contents, a tag spelling, a front-matter fence or a declared version range
neverActivates.reason: a dialect needs a resolved version or a named on profile (VID0 R08: activation reads the resolved installed version, never the declared range)

association.owner: LIQP0 owns document selectors and CLI globs (framework-template-carrier Surfaces); LIQ1G owns the client language contribution
association.rule: A .liquid file takes the mode of the one active Liquid claim whose scope contains it. Claims are the scopes of AP-S1..AP-S4 that are active for the file's package or ancestors.
association.needSelection: A file inside the scopes of two claims naming different semantic profiles is NeedSelection: different modes (for example a theme root inside a Jekyll site, a Jekyll Gemfile.lock and an Eleventy package over one directory, or an Eleventy package that also declares liquidjs directly), or one mode at two different exact releases (for example nested Gemfile.lock files resolving jekyll 4.4.0 and 4.4.1, or overlapping liquidjs claims resolving 10.29.0 and 10.30.0; each release is its own profile identity, docs/arch/kernel/identities.md). It gets no Liquid parse in either profile, no facts, and an explain output naming both claims. Only AP-S5 naming one profile resolves it. Registration order, nesting depth, load order or recency never decides (VID0 R10).
association.sameModeClaims: Two claims over one file are one claim only when they decode to the same profile at the same exact release (one semantic profile identity). The same mode at different exact releases is two claims and NeedSelection; the nearest scope never supplies the release.

explain: Every outcome carries its provenance (explicit, theme-root, lockfile, manifest, none) for the FWA1 explain output (LIQP0-AC1).
